items.title: Interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS traced to cold, ancient corner of the Milky Way

featured_image.name: Interstellar object Comet 3I/ATLAS leaving the solar system

items.description:
A comet that streaked through our solar system from another star likely originated in a frigid, remote region of the galaxy that had yet to form its own planetary system, astronomers announced on Thursday.

Comet 3I/ATLAS, only the third confirmed interstellar visitor and quite possibly the oldest, may be up to 11 billion years old — more than twice the age of our sun, according to the study published in Nature Astronomy.[1][2]

items.title: U.S.-Iran peace talks stall as Hormuz standoff pushes oil past $100

featured_image.name: Oil prices rise as US extends ceasefire, puts peace talks on hold

items.description:
Crude oil prices climbed sharply this week, with Brent crude breaking back above $100 per barrel on Wednesday, as an extended but fragile ceasefire between the United States and Iran failed to ease a mounting maritime standoff in the Strait of Hormuz that continues to choke global energy supplies.

Brent crude rose approximately 3.5 percent on Wednesday to $101.91 per barrel, according to The New York Times, while West Texas Intermediate crude edged up to $92.96. The gains followed a volatile stretch that saw prices jump roughly 5 percent on Tuesday amid uncertainty over the ceasefire's expiration, according to The National.[1][2]

items.title: Trump says China helped push Iran toward ceasefire talks

featured_image.name: Trump says he believes China got Iran to negotiate, AFP reports ...

items.description:
As the war between the United States, Israel, and Iran grinds through its second month, China has quietly positioned itself as a pivotal diplomatic player, leveraging its economic ties with Tehran and its desire for global leadership to carve out an outsized role in mediation efforts.

Chinese President Xi Jinping this week called for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz during a phone call with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on Monday, reaffirming Beijing's commitment to "all efforts conducive to restoring peace". The intervention followed weeks of intensive behind-the-scenes diplomacy. China's top diplomat Wang Yi made 26 phone calls between the start of the conflict on February 28 and the lead-up to the April 8 ceasefire, according to Al Jazeera.[1][2]
